questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Stop — come to a complete stop
questions.explain: A red octagon with white STOP means come to a full stop and proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.q: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign usually mean?
options: Warning of a hazard or condition ahead
questions.explain: Yellow diamonds are general warning signs. Slow down and prepare for the hazard shown.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: A red and white downward-pointing triangle is a YIELD sign. Slow, prepare to stop, and give way.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: A red circle with a horizontal white bar means Do Not Enter.

questions.q: A red circle with a diagonal slash through a symbol means…
questions.explain: Regulatory prohibition: the action (U-turn, left turn, etc.) is not allowed.

questions.q: What does this fluorescent yellow-green pentagon indicate?
questions.explain: The fluorescent yellow-green pentagon marks school zones and school crosswalks. Max 50 km/h when children are present unless otherwise posted.

questions.q: Orange diamond or rectangular signs generally indicate…
questions.explain: Orange is reserved for construction and maintenance. Expect workers, lane shifts, and lower speeds.

questions.q: A white rectangular sign with black lettering is typically…
questions.explain: White rectangles state the law: speed, parking, turns, one-way, etc.

questions.q: At a railway crossing with lights and bells activated, stop at least how far from the nearest rail?
questions.explain: Stop at least 5 m (16 ft) from the nearest rail. Do not proceed until signals stop and the way is clear.

questions.q: What does a chevron (arrowhead) alignment sign tell you?
options: Follow the direction of the curve
questions.explain: Chevrons mark a sharp curve or turn. Follow the direction they point.

questions.q: What colour is used for tourist / service information signs?
questions.explain: Blue signs mark motorist services and tourist attractions.

questions.q: What does a green circle (or green arrow) on a sign generally indicate?
questions.explain: Green often marks permitted movements or directional guidance.

questions.q: A yellow diamond with a traffic signal symbol means…
options: Traffic signals ahead — be prepared to stop
questions.explain: Warns that traffic control signals are ahead. Be ready to stop.

questions.q: A yellow diamond showing two arrows splitting around an obstacle means…
options: Divided highway begins / keep right of median
questions.explain: You are approaching a divided section; keep to the right of the median or island.

questions.q: What shape is a STOP sign?
questions.explain: Stop signs are always red octagons with white lettering.

questions.q: A white X-shaped railway crossing sign means…
options: Stop only if a train is visible
Railway crossing ahead / at the crossing
questions.explain: The crossbuck marks a railway crossing. Look and listen; stop if a train is approaching.

questions.q: A yellow diamond with a curved arrow and a side road symbol warns of…
options: A curve with a side road entering
questions.explain: Warning that a side road joins the main road within a curve — extra caution.

questions.q: A ‘No Right Turn on Red’ sign means…
options: You may turn after a full stop
Right turns on red are prohibited here
questions.explain: Even after a full stop, you may not turn right on red where this sign is posted.

questions.q: True or False: You may turn right on a red light after a full stop unless a sign prohibits it.
questions.explain: In New Brunswick you may turn right on red after stopping and yielding, unless prohibited by sign.

questions.q: A yellow diamond with pedestrians means…
questions.explain: Warns of a pedestrian crossing. Slow and be ready to stop.

questions.q: A rectangular white sign reading ‘MINIMUM 60’ means…
options: You must not drive slower than 60 km/h under normal conditions
questions.explain: Minimum speed signs require you not to drive below the posted speed when conditions allow.

questions.q: Lane-use control signs (arrows over lanes) tell you…
options: Which movements are allowed from that lane
questions.explain: They are regulatory: the arrows show the only permitted movements from that lane.

questions.q: A red octagon always means…
questions.explain: Only the STOP sign uses the red octagon shape.

questions.q: When approaching a railway crossing without gates or lights you must…
options: Slow, look and listen both ways, and be prepared to stop
questions.explain: Always approach uncontrolled crossings with extreme caution.

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, the default speed limit in urban districts in NB is…
questions.explain: Default is 50 km/h in urban districts and 80 km/h outside them unless posted otherwise.

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, the default speed limit outside urban areas is…
questions.explain: Outside urban districts the default is 80 km/h.

questions.q: You must signal a turn or lane change at least how far in advance?
questions.explain: Signal at least 30 m (about 100 ft) before turning or changing lanes.

questions.q: When an emergency or service vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, you must…
options: Slow to half the posted speed and move over if safe
Only slow if workers are present
questions.explain: NB Move Over law: reduce to half the posted limit, proceed with caution, change lanes away if safe.

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection when two vehicles arrive at about the same time, yield to…
questions.explain: Yield to the vehicle on your right.

questions.q: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing, stop at least…
questions.explain: Stop at least 5 m from the bus and remain stopped until the lights stop and the bus moves.

questions.q: Do not follow a fire apparatus responding to an emergency closer than…
questions.explain: Stay at least 150 m behind a fire apparatus answering an alarm.

questions.q: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels…
questions.explain: Uphill + curb: wheels left so the car rolls into the curb if brakes fail. Set the parking brake.

questions.q: True or False: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign even if the way looks clear.
questions.explain: A full stop is required every time.

questions.q: A solid yellow line on your side of the centre line means…
questions.explain: Solid yellow on your side = no passing. Broken yellow = passing when safe and legal.

questions.q: How far from a fire hydrant must you stay when parking?
questions.explain: Do not park within 5 m of a fire hydrant.

questions.q: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, you should…
options: Ease off the accelerator and steer straight
questions.explain: Ease off the gas and keep the wheel straight until the tires grip again.

questions.q: When a wheel runs off the pavement, first…
options: Ease off the accelerator and steer straight
questions.explain: Reduce speed gently, stay straight, then ease back onto the pavement when safe.

questions.q: Report a collision to police if there is injury/death or property damage of at least…
questions.explain: Report if death, injury, or damage of $1,000 or more. Always stop and exchange info.

questions.q: True or False: Radar detectors are legal in New Brunswick.
questions.explain: Radar detectors are illegal in New Brunswick.

questions.q: In a multi-lane roundabout you should…
options: Enter when safe, drive counter-clockwise, stay in your lane
questions.explain: Yield to traffic in the circle, enter when safe, stay in lane, exit carefully.

questions.q: Speeding fines in school zones and construction zones are…
questions.explain: Fines are doubled in school and construction zones.

questions.q: When backing up you should…
options: Back at walking speed while scanning and checking blind spots
questions.explain: Walking speed, continuous scan, mirrors and shoulder checks.

questions.q: Do not park within how many metres of a railway crossing?
questions.explain: No parking within 15 m of a railway crossing.

questions.q: True or False: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is signalling left, if safe.
questions.explain: Allowed in limited cases: vehicle signalling left, multi-lane same direction, one-way streets.

questions.q: Drivers and passengers must wear seatbelts. Drivers are responsible for passengers under…
questions.explain: The driver is responsible for ensuring passengers under 16 are properly restrained.

questions.q: Child seats / booster seats are required until the child reaches…
options: Age 9, 36 kg, or 145 cm (whichever comes first)
questions.explain: Until age 9, 36 kg (79 lb), or 145 cm (57 in), whichever comes first.

questions.q: On a two-way left-turn lane (shared centre lane) you may…
options: Drive the full block in it
Use it only to prepare for and complete a left turn
questions.explain: Use the centre left-turn lane only to enter/exit left turns — not as a through lane.

questions.q: When approaching a hillcrest where vision is limited you should…
questions.explain: Keep right and slow — oncoming traffic may be in your lane on the other side.

questions.q: True or False: You must dim high beams within 150 m of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.explain: Dim within 150 m of oncoming traffic and when following within 60 m.

questions.q: The basic speed rule means you must drive…
options: At a speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions
questions.explain: Even under the posted limit, speed must be safe for weather, traffic, and road conditions.

questions.q: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to stop should…
options: Always go first if from the right
Proceed first when it is their turn after stopping
questions.explain: First to stop goes first; if simultaneous, yield to the right.

questions.q: Pedestrians in a marked crosswalk have…
questions.explain: Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and at corners with sidewalks.

questions.q: When a tire blows out you should…
options: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off gas, steer straight
questions.explain: Grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, pull off when controlled.

questions.q: Parking is prohibited within how many metres of an intersection?
questions.explain: Do not park within 10 m of an intersection (check local bylaws; handbook stresses clear sight lines).

questions.q: True or False: It is illegal to drive with a hand-held electronic device in NB.
questions.explain: Hand-held device use while driving is prohibited. Graduated drivers face even stricter rules.

questions.q: Minimum age to apply for a Class 7 Level 1 learner’s licence in NB?
questions.explain: Minimum age is 16. Under 18 requires parental/guardian consent.

questions.q: True or False: A Level 1 learner must always be accompanied by a fully licensed supervising driver.
questions.explain: The supervisor must hold Class 5+ with at least 3 years experience and sit in the front passenger seat.

questions.q: During Level 1, driving is prohibited between…
questions.explain: Level 1: no driving from midnight to 5:00 a.m.

questions.q: True or False: Level 1 drivers may have BAC up to 0.05%.
questions.explain: Zero alcohol (0% BAC) for Level 1 at all times.

questions.q: Minimum time on Level 1 before the Level 2 road test?
questions.explain: 12 months, or 8 months after graduating a recognized licensed driving school.

questions.q: On Level 1, who may sit in the front passenger seat?
questions.explain: Only the qualified supervising driver may occupy the front passenger seat.

questions.q: True or False: Level 1 drivers may use hands-free devices while driving.
questions.explain: No electronic devices — including hands-free — for Level 1 drivers.

questions.q: Everyone in a Level 1 driver’s vehicle must…
questions.explain: All occupants must be seatbelted.

questions.q: Level 2 (intermediate) still requires…
options: Zero BAC and passenger limits that ease over time
questions.explain: Graduated rules continue: zero alcohol and staged passenger restrictions apply.

questions.q: Drivers under 21 in New Brunswick must maintain…
questions.explain: As of June 1, 2009, motorists under 21 must maintain 0% BAC while driving.

questions.q: True or False: You need to pass a vision screening as well as the written test for Level 1.
questions.explain: Vision screening and the knowledge test are both required.

questions.q: The supervising driver for Level 1 must have at least how many years of experience?
questions.explain: At least 3 years of driving experience on a full licence (Class 5 or higher).

questions.q: If a Level 1 driver is convicted of certain serious offences, the result can be…
options: Suspension / restart of the graduated period
questions.explain: Serious violations can suspend the licence and reset progress in the graduated system.

questions.q: True or False: Level 1 allows unlimited passengers as long as seatbelts exist.
questions.explain: Passenger rules are restricted; the front seat is for the supervisor only.

questions.q: The written knowledge test is based on…
options: The official New Brunswick Driver’s Handbook
questions.explain: Study the official handbook from Service NB / Public Safety.

questions.q: When entering a highway from a ramp you should…
options: Stop at the end of the ramp always
Match the speed of traffic and merge when safe
Expect others to always move over
questions.explain: Use the acceleration lane to match speed and merge with a gap.

questions.q: A flashing red traffic light means…
options: Treat it as a stop sign
questions.explain: Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe — same as a stop sign.

questions.q: A flashing amber (yellow) light means…
questions.explain: Slow and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.q: On a green arrow you may…
options: Proceed in the direction of the arrow, protected from conflicting traffic
questions.explain: A green arrow gives a protected movement in that direction.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: U-turn prohibited.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: Warning that the road ahead carries traffic in both directions.

questions.q: True or False: You must stop for a school bus with alternating flashing red lights on an undivided road, both directions.
questions.explain: On undivided roads, traffic both ways must stop. On divided highways, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

questions.q: The two-second rule (or more in poor conditions) helps you…
questions.explain: Pick a fixed point; you should reach it at least two seconds after the vehicle ahead.

questions.q: When driving in fog you should…
options: Use low beams and reduce speed
questions.explain: Low beams reduce glare; slow down and increase following distance.

questions.q: After passing the road test you receive…
questions.explain: Level 2 still has graduated restrictions before full Class 5.

questions.q: True or False: It is legal to leave a child under 12 alone in a vehicle if the weather is fine.
questions.explain: Never leave young children unattended in a vehicle — heat, cold, and other risks are serious.
